c.tagline: Fujian's island city of colonial Gulangyu, sea breezes, and oolong tea.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥10; most locals hail rides or pay via Didi and mobile QR (Alipay/WeChat), and some drivers may not accept foreign cards or make change for large notes.

emergency.note: 110 for police, 120 for ambulance/medical, and 119 for fire. English-speaking operators may be limited; hotel staff can help translate.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets and 'tea ceremony' overcharging scams in crowded spots like Zhongshan Road and the Gulangyu ferry queues.

hood_desc: The walkable old-town core around Zhongshan Road pedestrian street, the Gulangyu ferry piers, Shapowei fishing harbor, and Bailuzhou; the best base for first-timers who want sights, seafood, and the waterfront all within reach.

Gulangyu, the UNESCO-listed car-free island of colonial villas, the piano museum, and winding leafy lanes; an atmospheric, romantic stay for those who don't mind carrying luggage on foot and want the island to themselves after the day-trippers leave.
A laid-back seaside strip beside Xiamen University and the ring-road beaches, packed with hostels, cafes, murals, and cheap eats; suits students, backpackers, and beach-goers.
A modern commercial district around SM City Plaza and Jiahe Road with easy metro, BRT, and ferry connections; good for shoppers, business travelers, and anyone who values convenient transit.

A quieter mainland district across the bridge known for the Jimei School Village, Chen Jiageng's heritage architecture, and Jimei University; cheaper and more local, good for travelers wanting everyday Fujian life and heritage.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with BRT and main bus lines on similar hours and only limited night buses. Gulangyu ferries run day and night on a reduced overnight schedule.
transit.note: Xiamen has a growing metro network, an elevated BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) busway, extensive city buses, and frequent passenger ferries to Gulangyu Island.
transit.pay: Pay with the Xiamen e-Tong transit card, a QR code through Alipay/WeChat, or contactless; single metro rides run about ¥2-¥5 and buses ¥1-¥2. Foreign visitors can link an international card to Alipay or WeChat to pay by QR.

bus: Intercity coaches to Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and Fuzhou

car.idp: Not recognized (a Chinese driving license is required)

ferry: Ferries to Gulangyu Island (from Lundu and Dongdu terminals)
train: Xiamen Railway Station and Xiamen North Railway Station (high-speed rail to Fuzhou, Shenzhen, and Shanghai)

transit.m: Airport bus / BRT connection to city center (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; a service charge may be added at high-end hotels and restaurants.

landmarks: Gulangyu Island
A car-free island of colonial mansions, winding lanes, and piano museums, Gulangyu is a UNESCO World Heritage site and Xiamen's most photographed destination.
Nanputuo Temple
This centuries-old Buddhist temple at the foot of Wulao Peak draws pilgrims and photographers with its incense-filled courtyards and mountain backdrop.
Xiamen University
Widely called China's most beautiful campus, its lakeside gardens and red-roofed buildings make it a favorite spot for students and visiting tourists alike.
Sunlight Rock (Riyanguang Yan)
The highest point on Gulangyu Island, this granite boulder rewards climbers with sweeping panoramic views over Xiamen's harbor and skyline.
Hulishan Fortress
Home to the world's largest 19th-century coastal cannon, this Qing dynasty fort blends military history with dramatic ocean-facing ramparts.
Shuzhuang Garden
An elegant seaside garden on Gulangyu Island featuring the famous Piano Museum, ornamental bridges, and pavilions overlooking the sea.
Zhongshan Road Pedestrian Street
Xiamen's bustling historic shopping street, lined with arcaded colonial-era buildings, is beloved for its lively nightlife and street food.
Xiamen Botanical Garden
Sprawling across Wanshi Mountain, this garden's misty rainforest zone and rare plant collections make it a lush escape from the city.
Jimei School Village
Founded by philanthropist Tan Kah Kee, this striking blend of Chinese and Western architecture honors his legacy with grand halls and monuments.
White Egret Island Park
A tranquil downtown park set on an islet in Yundang Lake, known for its egret statues, sunset views, and skyline photography.

train.note: No trains cross an international border from Xiamen; the cross-strait link to Taiwan is by boat or plane. Xiamen North station (on the island's mainland side, reached by metro and shuttle trains) handles most high-speed departures, while the rebuilt Xiamen station in the city serves some G- and D-trains. Since the Fuzhou-Xiamen high-speed railway opened in September 2023, Fuzhou is about an hour away, Shenzhen around three hours and Shanghai roughly five. Book on 12306 with your passport and allow time to reach Xiamen North, which is well outside the old town.

bus.note: There are no international coach services from Xiamen. Domestic long-distance buses use the Hubin, Songbai and Jimei terminals, with services around Fujian to Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, Wuyishan and inland Jiangxi, but high-speed rail has taken over most of these corridors. Tickets are sold at terminal counters and via Chinese apps; bring your passport. Allow 30-45 minutes across the causeways in rush hour if your bus leaves from a mainland-side terminal.

intl.to: Kinmen (Taiwan) - 30-60 min crossing from Wutong Ferry Terminal, with full immigration and Kinmen Airport check-in on site
intl.op: Xiamen-Kinmen "Mini Three Links" ferry — tickets sold at the Wutong terminal counter and Chinese travel agents; no official English booking site

intl.to: Gulangyu Island (China) - 5-20 min from Dongdu / Lundu piers

ferry.note: Wutong Ferry Terminal in the northeast of Xiamen Island is the mainland end of the cross-strait "Mini Three Links" to Kinmen, roughly hourly through the day and taking about half an hour to an hour; foreign passport holders may use it, but you clear mainland exit formalities and then Taiwanese entry formalities on Kinmen, so treat it as a full border crossing. A second historic route runs from Quanzhou's Shuitou pier to Kinmen. Services have been repeatedly suspended and restored since 2020, so confirm sailings before you build a trip around them. Separately, Xiamen Ferry Co. runs the constant short hop to Gulangyu Island from the Dongdu and Lundu piers, which visitors must book online in advance because daily visitor numbers are capped.

half.name: Quanzhou
half.blurb: Historic maritime Silk Road port city with old mosques, temples, and a still-active traditional shipbuilding district.

half.name: Zhangzhou
half.blurb: Nearby city known for its old riverside town, flower and fruit markets, and traditional red-brick architecture.

full.name: Fujian Tulou (Yongding/Nanjing)
full.blurb: UNESCO-listed circular earthen buildings built by Hakka clans, some housing hundreds of families under one roof.
